defects.description: The ingestion DLQ is defined and monitored, but neither a source-queue redrive policy nor a queue-to-DLQ relationship is specified. Configure the DLQ ARN and maxReceiveCount so repeatedly failing messages actually reach the monitored queue.

Authentication is specified, but customer-scoped authorization for conversation history is not. Derive ownership from the validated customer identity, enforce it on every history operation, and define least-privilege access for the chat and ingestion roles.

DynamoDB TTL does not guarantee physical deletion exactly at 30 days. Clarify the retention interpretation, exclude expired records from conversation reads, and provide additional deletion controls if 30 days is a strict purge deadline.

The Cognito-to-API invocation arrow misrepresents authorization: the customer supplies a token and API Gateway's configured authorizer validates it. The history read arrow also uses the opposite operation direction from the other read edges.

The usage-scale and availability clarification requirements remain questions rather than concrete architectural assumptions; specify these before sizing OpenSearch and setting ingestion concurrency and service quotas.

reviews.summary: The managed RAG design covers the requested functionality, but customer-level authorization, ingestion redrive configuration, and retention semantics need clarification before implementation.

defects.description: The sole change-capture path is an Aurora 'Stream' directly triggering Lambda, but Aurora does not provide the native Lambda stream event-source mapping implied here. Aurora-to-Lambda invocation integrations are not automatic CDC streams. Specify a supported CDC pipeline or an explicit trigger/outbox consumer, including initial loading and measured end-to-end lag, before claiming sub-minute search freshness.

The design describes a second ALB as required for multi-AZ operation and places each ALB in only one subnet. A regional ALB requires subnets in at least two Availability Zones; two independent single-subnet ALBs are not a valid substitute. Represent one logical ALB associated with both public subnets.

The cache has only a read path. No population on cache miss, refresh, TTL, or invalidation behavior is specified, leaving the high-read product-page optimization incomplete and potentially stale after updates.

The search index is placed only in AZ-a with no multi-AZ or replica configuration, while all API tasks are also shown only in AZ-a. Database Multi-AZ alone does not make browsing and search resilient to an AZ failure.
Private placement and HTTPS ingress are useful, but task-role permissions, security-group relationships, database/cache transport encryption, and OpenSearch access policies are unspecified.

CloudWatch is disconnected from the workload, and no synchronization-lag alarm, replay strategy, or indexing-failure handling is described. Traffic and availability assumptions also remain unanswered clarification questions.

Requiring Cognito sign-in before shoppers can browse or search is an unrequested product constraint and adds authentication complexity; mark this as an assumption or restrict authentication to operations that require it.

reviews.summary: The service choices broadly fit product search, but the unsupported CDC stream and incorrect per-AZ ALB model make the stated implementation non-working.

defects.description: Public-subnet placement alone does not give a Fargate task outbound connectivity. Specify an assigned public IP and internet-gateway route, or appropriate private endpoints/egress, so the task can pull its image and reach logging, S3, and SES services; inbound access need not be opened.

The task's AWS permissions are not defined. Specify a least-privilege task role for report-prefix S3 operations, presigned GET authorization, and SES sending, separate from the execution role used for task startup and logging.

Failure visibility is planned, but runtime retry/rerun behavior and idempotency are unspecified. Distinguish successful task launch from successful report completion, and prevent duplicate reports or emails when a run is repeated.
Choose an explicit presigned-link lifetime and account for expiration of the task-role credentials used to sign it; retaining reports for a year does not make an emailed link valid for a year.

The existing Aurora database's encryption state, database TLS requirements, and secure credential retrieval are not stated; verify these rather than treating private-subnet placement as the complete data-protection control.

reviews.summary: Scheduled Fargate, private S3 lifecycle storage, and SES form a simple low-cost solution for the 25-minute job, with networking, permissions, and rerun details still required.

reviews.summary: The design appropriately uses scheduled Fargate for the long-running job and explicitly encrypted storage, while leaving networking, permissions, and rerun behavior to be completed.

preference.why: Both have the same functional architecture and implementation gaps; A's explicit S3 and DynamoDB encryption labels do not materially distinguish services that encrypt stored data by default.
B avoids A's unnecessary second ALB and unrequested shopper-authentication dependency, but neither design is buildable as specified until the Aurora CDC path is corrected.

B has a narrow security-specification advantage by explicitly requiring Aurora encryption while preserving the same simple, inexpensive scheduled-Fargate workflow; both need the same networking and permission fixes.
